text:
“I haven’t lived this derby,” Andoni Iraola acknowledged, and yet he already feels it. A former Athletic Bilbao captain coming up against an ex-Real Sociedad head coach needs no instruction on the importance of winning a derby, whether in the Basque country or on Merseyside. But this week, as the Liverpool head coach approaches his first experience of the latter, there has been no escape.
“It has been very easy for me here,” says Iraola of his five months on Merseyside. “Family-wise we have settled in really well. People here are very friendly, they love to talk to you but in a very respectful way. This week there has been a lot [of interaction with Liverpool fans], especially with playing big games against United and Everton. ‘We need to win, we need to win,’ they say.”
That has rarely been a problem of late for Liverpool, who have lost one of their past 15 visits to Everton and showed with last season’s 100th-minute winner from Virgil van Dijk that a move to a new stadium does not necessarily mean a fresh start.
Iraola has identified parallels with the Basque derby not only through this week’s encounters with an approving public. The Liverpool head coach says of Athletic v Sociedad: “It is a massive game for us and it’s a bit like here – you know a lot of people on the other side. I have a lot of friends who are Real Sociedad and they have a lot of friends who are Athletic. I think it’s quite a natural rivalry. The relationship between them is normally quite good but everyone wants to win that game.”
David Moyes, who managed Real Sociedad for 12 months from November 2014, offers a comparison that extends beyond football. “In some ways, the Basques are like scousers,” the Everton manager says. “They compete with each other and they are rivals but they see themselves as being different from the rest of the country. There is a bit of camaraderie between them. But it is a fierce derby and a huge game.
“The thing about Real Sociedad, nearly all your players have to be Basque. Bilbao are pure Basque but we had incredible players coming through ourselves. We gave a debut to [Mikel] Oyarzabal. They had an incredible setup. There are very few teams in the Premier League who could do what Sociedad do in terms of bringing kids through the ranks.”
Moyes had a habit of frustrating but not beating his local rivals during his time in the Basque country, which has echoes of his record in the Merseyside derby. That reads four wins, nine draws and 16 defeats across two spells with Everton. All three of his games in charge of Real Sociedad versus Athletic ended in draws, with the first two featuring a red card. Iraola played in the second, in April 2015, when La Real had a man sent off but fought back to draw 1-1 at San Mamés in the last of his 12 seasons with his boyhood club.
Despite being born only 10km from San Sebastián, and 100km from Bilbao, there was no question which Basque club Iraola was destined to represent. “It was always Athletic for me,” he says. “I went there very young and I never played for the academy of Real Sociedad. I have a lot of friends who went on to play for Real Sociedad but at my club, Antiguoko, in that moment and also now, it was like an Athletic Club team. The connections mean if you are good at Antiguoko you will go through the Athletic Club system. I was lucky enough to arrive there and spend 16 years in Bilbao.”
The Merseyside rivals enter the 249th edition of England’s most-played derby on the back of starkly contrasting weeks. Whereas Everton suffered the heaviest defeat of Moyes’s second spell as manager in Monday’s 4-0 hammering at Brentford, where they also produced arguably their worst performance since the Scot’s return, Liverpool have plundered seven goals without reply in commanding victories against Manchester United and Club Brugge. Their away form under Iraola also augurs well for a fourth successive win over Everton for the first time since a run to August 1991.
Liverpool have won their past four fixtures on the road and six from eight in all competitions, scoring 21 times. And it is not only their pace, Florian Wirtz’s growing influence and Alexander Isak’s predatory qualities in attack that have made the difference away from Anfield. No team have conceded fewer goals on their travels in the Premier League this season than Liverpool, with four. The additions of Jérémy Jacquet and Ronald Araújo have improved Liverpool’s resilience as well as their defending at set pieces, both of which will be important at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday.
“I don’t think there is a big difference in our performances away or at home,” Iraola says. “Normally you will find more spaces when you play away because teams are braver and they press you more. But sometimes they can press you and you will feel more uncomfortable. I prefer to play at home even if we have better numbers away at the moment. Also at home we have had difficult games in terms of having big games, but the way we play doesn’t really change a lot.
“Derbies are always different. It doesn’t matter where you are in the standings, it doesn’t matter the run that you are in. Normally, this type of game is different and you can feel it from the beginning. We have to be very competitive, we have to win our duels and be at a good level because everyone wants to win this game.”

מאמן ליברפול, אנדוני איראולה, מתכונן לקראת הדרבי הראשון שלו מול אברטון ודייוויד מויס. איראולה, קפטן אתלטיק בילבאו לשעבר, מוצא קווי דמיון בין היריבות הבסקים המפורסמת לבין המפגש הקרוב במרסיסייד, ומציין כי האווירה והיריבות הספורטיבית טבעיות מאוד לשני המקרים.

מנגד, מויס, שאימן בעבר את ריאל סוסיאדד, משווה בין האופי הבסקי לזה של תושבי ליברפול, ומציין את התשוקה והמחויבות הגדולה למשחקים מסוג זה. שתי הקבוצות מגיעות לדרבי ה-249 במצב רוח שונה, כאשר ליברפול רושמת רצף משחקים מרשים והגנה יציבה, בעוד אברטון מנסה להתאושש מהפסד צורב.

איראולה מדגיש את החשיבות של התחרותיות במשחקי דרבי, בהם המיקום בטבלה או הכושר הנוכחי אינם קובעים דבר. לדבריו, הקבוצה תצטרך להיות במיטבה, להילחם על כל כדור ולשמור על רמת ביצוע גבוהה כדי לצאת עם תוצאה חיובית.
